Open-Source Windows Download Manager 'Awesome-Downloader' Released in Early Preview

Overview of Awesome-Downloader

A new open-source Windows download manager named Awesome-Downloader has been released as an early preview. The project features a compact desktop interface alongside browser video integration. According to the available repository information, the software is an original open-source implementation and is not affiliated with Internet Download Manager (IDM), nor does it aim to be a complete feature-for-feature replacement.

Core Features and Capabilities

The preview release includes several practical capabilities for general file management and media handling:

  • Standard Transfers: Supports HTTP(S) downloads with parallel ranges where servers permit, alongside pause, resume, history, scheduling, and speed limits.
  • Media Detection: Integrates with Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera to detect media, offer quality selection, and combine video and audio locally using FFmpeg.
  • File Management: Provides download file info with save location settings, categories, a 'Download Later' option, and start or cancel controls.
  • Window Management: Features separate progress and completion windows, along with duplicate active download prevention.
  • YouTube Handling: Utilizes captured browser-session data and the GoogleVideo SABR transport library for specific video handling. The developers note this is an experimental feature rather than a guarantee of universal site support or DRM circumvention.

Current Preview Limitations

Users evaluating the early preview should note several operational boundaries and security considerations:

  • Unsupported Content: Private or sign-in-required content, DRM-protected media, and live streams are not supported.
  • Installation Status: The Windows installer is currently unsigned. Browser video buttons require a manual 'Load unpacked' setup because official browser-store listings are not yet available.
  • Browser Parity: Firefox YouTube capture support has not yet reached parity with Chromium-based browsers.
  • Data Handling: Media request credentials are kept strictly in memory and are never stored in the download history. Local configuration and history are stored within `%USERPROFILE%\.awesome-downloader`, and the internal bridge is authenticated and loopback-only.

Development and Verification

Developers can build the application locally using Node.js commands such as `npm run package` or `npm run dist` for an NSIS installer. Version 0.1.1 and later include a GitHub Releases update checker that prompts users before downloading or restarting.

To verify the original announcement, review the code, or report bugs safely without exposing session tokens, interested parties can visit the official GitHub repository at Ahmadkhattak1/awesome-downloader.
